findings.title: Task 3.4 mandates 'fresh-sandbox install' but never defines what 'sandbox' is
findings.details: After FF4 stripped the escape hatch, task 3.4 reads 'Mandatory: run a fresh-sandbox install per the documented README sequence'. But 'fresh sandbox' is undefined — temp dir? Docker? fresh git clone? specific Node version? Different interpretations produce different file counts. Implementing AI may default to escalation (defeating FF4 intent) or interpret 'sandbox' loosely (re-running install in dev tree — not actually fresh).
findings.recommendation: Define 'fresh sandbox' inline. Minimum: temp directory + same Node version as project's package.json + run openspec init from clean state. One parenthetical sentence in task 3.4.

findings.title: orbit's archive dependency on openspec-sync-specs primitive not anchored as normative requirement
findings.line: Overlay file disposition, Upstream-required primitive scenario
findings.details: Overlay file disposition says 'kept verbatim because orbit depends on it as a callable primitive' but doesn't anchor WHICH orbit code calls it. Implementation evidence (openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md:65,112,123) confirms archive flow invokes openspec-sync-specs via subagent, but only as prose, not normative spec. If Option 2 (#27) work rewrites archive flow without re-reading those SKILL.md invocation specifics, sync-specs could be quietly dropped — making 'Upstream-required primitive' rationale orphaned. Then someone could prune sync-specs as another feedback-class candidate without realizing they broke archive.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add normative requirement to orbit-conventions OR orbit-archive-modifications capturing the dependency ('orbit's archive flow depends on openspec-sync-specs as a callable primitive invoked via subagent; the primitive MUST remain available in the overlay as long as the archive flow uses it'); or (b) cross-reference openspec-archive-change/SKILL.md invocation pattern from the Upstream-required primitive scenario for traceability.

findings.title: 'post-pegging forward-looking framing' prescription is subjective
findings.details: Requirement says Identity SHALL convey 'post-pegging forward-looking framing'. The Workflow-tool framing scenario gives one example pattern but the constraint is otherwise loose. Two implementing AIs could produce semantically-different content that both technically satisfy the spec.
findings.recommendation: Tighten with negative test: 'framing MUST NOT use augmentation language (e.g., "augments cleanly", "overlay on top of", "layered on top of upstream")'. Negative test more useful than positive — goal is preventing old framing, not enforcing specific new vocabulary.

findings.title: Try-it nudge assumes user has a real project idea
findings.details: Nudge prescribes /opsx:explore <name> 'on a real project idea they have', 'for practice' explicitly avoided. Constraint-probe: orientation-only users (collaborators new to orbit, AI sessions getting context cold) have no concrete idea yet. They get a recommendation they can't act on.
findings.recommendation: Relax to: 'recommend /opsx:explore <name> when the reader has a real idea, OR /opsx:explore (bare mode) to think out loud if no idea is ready yet'. Preserves no-demo-change discipline; surfaces bare-mode as the no-decision-yet entry point per orbit-explore conventions.
